newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-Desperation the key to Chch game -Preston.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-Desperation the key to Chch game -Preston.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Aug 18 - Wellington's one remaining All Black, Jon Preston, has called for "desperation" from his team in their opening NPC rugby game tonight in Christchurch, NZPA reports.

Taranaki's shock win over Auckland yesterday has set the cat among the pigeons in the battle for early points -- and removed any thoughts that the later match with Taranaki will be a straightforward win for Wellington.

Thus a good performance tonight at Lancaster Park and then a win against North Harbour on Saturday have become paramount demands for the Wellington Lions, who go into tonight's match without injured All Blacks Alama Ieremia and Tana Umaga.
Umaga is still having minor problems with his chest injury suffered in Johannesburg, and Ieremia suffered a haematoma on a calf when an Australian forward stood on him on Saturday.
Ieremia was in superb form and his loss is massive for Wellington.
The other problem could be coach Frank Walker's decision to fly the team in so late because he feels they get "bored" before a game.
The early afternoon flight may give players little time to recover.
Preston knows the team's poor early form hasn't been a reflection of the talent available.
"I think the guys having the three-day camp together (last week) will make a big difference, because it's been pretty difficult to get any unity with the amount of changes," Preston said.
"And I certainly hope there will be desperation to turn things around -- that hasn't been there at all in previous games."
It won't be easy for Wellington tonight. Even at the best of times Wellington have been beaten in Christchurch in recent years, and Canterbury are tipped for a top-four place.
All Black halfback Justin Marshall is missing, but Andrew Mehrtens is keen to get back into business and chase his No 1 All Black first five-eighth spot. It will be his 50th match for Canterbury.
There is immense attacking skill in the backline, behind a pack more solid than powerful.
Wellington captain Jason O'Halloran moves out to centre to allow newcomer Paul Steinmetz into second five-eighth.
